_comment: Descriptive regression floors, seeded from the deterministic OFFLINE harness on main (commit a78c3c2d). The offline corpus serves SCRIPTED reviewer findings, so these guard harness / scorer / dispatch correctness, NOT model quality. The `evals` CI job runs `evals/thresholds.py check` and fails when a metric regresses past a floor here. Update these deliberately, in the same PR, when the corpus changes; never invent an aspirational number (mirrors the mutation-threshold rule in references/gates.md). Live per-model baselines are committed after the first live calibration (the E1-S4 $20 run); see the runbook in evals/README.md.

live._comment: `evals/thresholds.py compare` flags any overall/per-category detection-rate drop greater than this fraction, and any model whose true-positive contribution fell, between two live calibration reports. Baseline: `evals/report/live-20260913-195628-10144.json` (first adopted baseline, 2026-09-13, reps=5, reproducible - per-rep model/role attribution + sha256 digest; supersedes the exploratory live-20260823-211755 reps=2 run; detection 100%, 22 FPs on the two clean cases). Run `compare` at reps=5 to match this baseline: detection-rate signals are rep-independent, but the per-model true-positive signal is a raw count and needs matching reps.
